correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from explicit 15-edge Petersen graph: exhaustive 1024-mask forest membership check yields 75,260,620,785 nonempty faces and prescribed face vectors. The full oriented Hasse graph is acyclic for exact element matchings of F0,F2,F3, leaving, after removing the augmented empty-face pair, one vertex and respectively 4 degree-2, 1 degree-3 and 6 degree-5 critical cells. For F2->F1 each of 180 deterministic pairs is a free codimension-one face and its unique facet at removal and the final complex is exactly F1. Morse and elementary-collapse theorems imply exact integral homotopy types and the maps in the claimed persistence diagram. Separate exact signed mod-p boundary ranks for primes 2,3,5,101 corroborate. No unsupported infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The published 2023 forest-filtration framework treats distinct families; its exact definitions were compared with this complete Petersen vertex filtration. Public Petersen F1~S3 notes already cover the middle-stage homotopy, and Berghoff covers F0 homology, but neither proves the concrete F2-to-F1 elementary collapse, the six 5-spheres in F_infty, or the integral persistence diagram. Successful published-finding corpus searches for multiple equivalent formulations and comparison to accessible own prior claims did not uncover stronger coverage; this is evidence-based originality with residual indexing risk, not absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The three-regular Petersen graph is a canonical smallest girth-five cubic example with cycles meeting, outside the families covered in the defining forest-filtration work. The new explicit F2 to F1 simple collapse identifies a nontrivial filtration plateau at the level of homotopy maps, while the terminal six 5-spheres and exact integral intervals quantify the subsequent jump. A natural complete classification of the published filtration on this benchmark graph is substantively motivated and not implied by the inherited F0/F1 endpoints.
